para-01-c1.quote: In 1957, the IBM Mathematical Formula Translating System, or Fortran, debuted.
para-01-c1.claim: Imperative programming is the original paradigm, born with Fortran in 1957.

para-01-c3.text: Edsger W. Dijkstra (1968). A Case against the GO TO Statement (EWD215). E.W. Dijkstra Archive, University of Texas at Austin.
para-01-c3.quote: The additions are absent from the typescript furnished to the archive but are present in the version published in Comm. ACM 11 (March 1968), 147–148 under the title “Go To Statement Considered Harmful”.
para-01-c3.claim: In 1968, Edsger Dijkstra published a one-page letter titled Go To Statement Considered Harmful.

para-02-c1.text: Milestones: Object-Oriented Programming, 1961-1967. IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki.
para-02-c1.quote: In the 1970s in USA, Alan Kay picked up the ideas of SIMULA in his Smalltalk language.
para-02-c1.claim: Object-oriented programming (OOP) emerged from Simula 67 and was crystallized by Smalltalk in the 1970s.

para-02-c2.text: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ). The Go Programming Language.
para-02-c2.quote: Although Go has types and methods and allows an object-oriented style of programming, there is no type hierarchy.
para-02-c2.claim: Languages like Go drop classical inheritance entirely; languages like Rust use traits (interfaces) without inheritance trees.

para-03-c1.text: A. M. Kuchling. Functional Programming HOWTO. Python documentation.
para-03-c1.quote: Functional style discourages functions with side effects that modify internal state or make other changes that aren’t visible in the function’s return value. Functions that have no side effects at all are called purely functional.
para-03-c1.claim: A pure function is one that, given the same inputs, always returns the same output, and has no observable effect beyond its return value.

para-03-c3.quote: Based on lambda calculus, Haskell is a purely functional programming language that features referential transparency, immutability and lazy evaluation.
para-03-c3.claim: Haskell uses lazy evaluation by default, which lets you write take 10 (filter isPrime [1..]): "the first 10 primes from the infinite list of all integers".

para-04-c1.quote: When programming in SQL you tell the system what you want to compute, not how to compute it. The task of figuring out the how is delegated to the query planner subsystem within the SQL database engine.
para-04-c1.claim: SELECT name FROM users WHERE age > 18 says nothing about how the query runs.

para-04-c3.quote: A MiniZinc model does not dictate how to solve the problem - the MiniZinc compiler can translate it into different forms suitable for a wide range of solvers, such as Constraint Programming (CP), Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MIP) or Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) solvers.
para-04-c3.claim: Languages like MiniZinc let you write var 1..9: x; var 1..9: y; constraint x + y == 13; constraint x < y; solve; and the solver finds (4,9), (5,8), (6,7).

para-05-c2.text: Carl Hewitt, Peter Bishop, Richard Steiger (1973). A Universal Modular ACTOR Formalism for Artificial Intelligence. Proceedings of the 3rd International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI).
para-05-c2.quote: This paper proposes a modular ACTOR architecture and definitional method for artificial intelligence
para-05-c2.claim: The actor model, introduced by Carl Hewitt in 1973, takes a different approach: there is no shared memory at all.

para-05-c3.text: C. A. R. Hoare (1978). Communicating Sequential Processes. Communications of the ACM.
para-05-c3.quote: This paper suggests that input and output are basic primitives of programming and that parallel composition of communicating sequential processes is a fundamental program structuring method.
para-05-c3.claim: Communicating Sequential Processes (CSP), formalized by Tony Hoare in 1978, is the actor model's twin.

para-05-c3.text: Effective Go. The Go Programming Language.
para-05-c3.quote: To encourage this way of thinking we have reduced it to a slogan: Do not communicate by sharing memory; instead, share memory by communicating.
para-05-c3.claim: Send and receive block until both sides meet: "don't communicate by sharing memory; share memory by communicating".
